recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not restore the older CodeableReference targets under FHIR-28584 unless BR&R opens a new issue to revisit the later one-way Ingredient and PackagedProductDefinition relationship decisions.
issue_request: FHIR-28584 was a Published/Persuasive R5 BR&R request to use CodeableReference for selected medication-definition ingredient and package relationships so simple codes could be used instead of full resources where appropriate.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied by git e9799080ee and 0ee3e67a82, which changed medication-definition source/example inputs for FHIR#28584 and adjacent CodeableReference work.
additional_context: Later Published BR&R decisions changed the same model: FHIR-31808 reversed Ingredient link direction, FHIR-31859 removed MedicinalProductDefinition-to-PackagedProductDefinition references, and FHIR-31782/FHIR-31596 history explains why the interim package backbone is no longer current. These later decisions are already represented on the combined branch.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current PackagedProductDefinition.packaging.containedItem.item is CodeableReference; MedicinalProductDefinition.ingredient and ManufacturedItemDefinition.ingredient are coded shortcuts with incoming Ingredient references for detailed modeling; MedicinalProductDefinition.packagedMedicinalProduct is a coded package type while PackagedProductDefinition.packageFor carries the full package-to-product relationship.
